title: Purification of 2,3-bisphosphate-dependent phosphoglycerate mutase (dPGM)
author: Cristina Rodrigues Gabriel Sales
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgawjsfe
materials: SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE JUST BEFORE USE Prepared with reagents/solutions described in step 1.
Ressuspend pellet with 3 mL buffer F.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare all necessary media and buffers for the purification process.

substeps.instruction: Prepare LB medium: 10 mg/mL Tryptone, 5 mg/mL Yeast extract, ultrapure H2O; adjust to pH 7 with NaOH; autoclave. For LB agar, add 10 mg/mL agar, melt in microwave, equilibrate at 50 °C for 30 min, add 100 ng/ml carbenicillin, pour 25 mL per plate, set for 25 min, and store at 4 °C for 2-3 weeks.
Prepare 100 mg/mL Carbenicillin: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, filter through 0.25 µm sterile syringe filter, store at 4 °C.
Prepare 0.1 M IPTG: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, aliquot, store at -20 °C.
Prepare Buffer A: 0.1 M Potassium phosphate, 75 mM NaCl in ultrapure H2O; adjust to pH 8 with NaOH, filter, store at 4 °C.
Prepare Buffer W (Washing): 100 mM Tris base, 150 mM NaCl in ultrapure H2O; adjust to pH 8 with HCl, filter, store at 4 °C.
Prepare Buffer F (Final): 60 mM Tris base in ultrapure H2O; adjust to pH 7.9 with HCl, filter, store at 4 °C.
Prepare 10 mM Leupeptin hemisulfate: Add 5.25 mL ethanol to 0.025 g powder, aliquot, store at -20 °C.
Prepare 100 mM PMSF: Dissolve in ethanol, store at 4 °C.
Prepare 4.5 M Ammonium sulfate: Dissolve powder in ultrapure H2O with mild heat, adjust to pH 7 with NH4OH, let precipitate, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Chromatography Columns
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the desalting and purification resins.

substeps.instruction: Sephadex G-25 fine: Swell 5 g resin in Buffer A for at least 3 hours at room temperature. Fill glass column to 20 mL bed volume and equilibrate with 3 column volumes of Buffer A.
Strep-Tactin Sepharose: Fill glass column with 20 mL bed volume (50% suspension in Buffer W). Equilibrate with 2 column bed volumes of Buffer W at 4 °C.

steps.title: Cell Growth and Collection
steps.instruction: Cultivate E. coli and collect cell pellets.

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Inoculate LB plates (100 ng/ml carbenicillin) with cells and incubate upside down overnight (~9h) at 37 °C.
Day 2: Pick a single colony and inoculate 10 mL LB (with 100 ng/ml carbenicillin) in a 50 mL Falcon tube; shake overnight (~9h) at 37 °C. (For larger cultures, use 4 tubes for 40 mL total).
Day 3: Prepare glycerol stock by mixing 300 µL culture with 300 µL 30% glycerol in a 2 mL screw-cap tube; store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Induction of dPGM Expression
steps.instruction: Induce protein expression and harvest cells.

substeps.instruction: Dilute culture 1:50 in a 1 L Erlenmeyer flask (20 mL culture in 1 L final volume).
Grow cells at 37 °C with continuous stirring at 225 rpm.
Monitor OD600; once it reaches approx. 0.8, remove a 1 mL aliquot for SDS-PAGE, centrifuge, and store supernatant at -20 °C.
Induce expression by adding 1 mL of 0.1 M IPTG to the 1 L culture.
Maintain culture at 29 °C overnight under continuous stirring.
Day 4: Transfer 400 mL culture to two 500 mL centrifuge bottles on ice.
Collect cells by centrifuging at 4000 rpm, 4 °C, for 10 minutes; discard supernatant.
Suspend pellets in ~20 mL Buffer A, distribute into 2x 50 mL screw cap tubes on ice. Rinse bottles with 5 mL Buffer A and add to tubes.
Centrifuge at 5000 x g, 4 °C, for 10 minutes; discard supernatant and dry pellets. Store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Cell Lysis
steps.instruction: Rupture cells to release soluble protein.

substeps.instruction: Day 5: Thaw pellets on ice (via -20 °C freeze-thaw cycle).
Suspend pellets in lysis buffer at a ratio of 5 mg/g wet cell pellet weight (e.g., 13.47 mL buffer for 2.694 g pellet).
Vortex and keep on ice.
Sonicate the suspension in a beaker on ice: apply 3 x 45s bursts with 30s pauses until the solution is easy to pipette.
Centrifuge at 26000 rpm, 4 °C, for 20 minutes; collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Initial Precipitation and Desalting
steps.instruction: Concentrate protein via ammonium sulfate precipitation and remove salts.

substeps.instruction: Add saturated ammonium sulfate drop-wise to the supernatant to reach 80% (v/v) saturation (Vol = (Vol supernatant / 0.2) - Vol supernatant) while stirring for 30 min.
Collect precipitate by centrifugation at 20000 x g, 4 °C, for 13 minutes (slow brake).
Resuspend pellets in 3 mL Buffer A on ice using a 1 mL pipette.
Centrifuge at 20000 x g, 4 °C, for 20 minutes to remove debris.
Equilibrate Sephadex G-25 column with 2 column volumes of Buffer A and 1 column volume of lysis buffer.
Load sample and elute with lysis buffer; pool fractions with highest protein content (monitored by Bradford reagent/blue color).
Wash the sample further by adding 5 mL Buffer A, then 2 mL elutions until protein content is low.
Clean column with 2 column volumes of 0.2 M NaOH, rinse with water, and re-equilibrate with 2-3 column volumes of Buffer A.

steps.title: Protein Purification and Final Polishing
steps.instruction: Purify dPGM using affinity chromatography and final desalting.

substeps.instruction: Purify dPGM using a Strep-tactin Sepharose 20 mL bed column according to manufacturer's instructions.
Perform a second precipitation: add saturated ammonium sulfate drop-wise to 80% (v/v) saturation, stir for 30 min, and centrifuge at 20000 x g, 4 °C, for 13 minutes (slow brake).
Resuspend the resulting pellet in 3 mL Buffer F.
Equilibrate Sephadex G-25 column with 3 column volumes of Buffer F.
Load sample and elute with Buffer F; pool fractions with highest protein content (typically fractions 3 to 6).
Clean column with 2 column volumes of 0.2 M NaOH, rinse with water, and re-equilibrate with 2-3 column volumes of Buffer A.
Store pooled fractions at -80 °C after verifying activity (3-PGA consumption with 2,3dPGA).
